title: A Beetle Makes Near-Boiling Spray Inside Its Own Body
subject: bombardier beetle

scenes.text: A beetle makes near-boiling spray inside its body. Somehow it survives.
Its glands store hydrogen peroxide and hydroquinone, two chemicals that react when mixed.
They stay apart until danger. Then both squeeze into a chamber full of enzymes.
The reaction heats the mix to nearly 100 degrees Celsius, about the boiling point of water.
It fires in pulses, around 500 times a second, at up to 22 miles an hour.
Its glands hold enough for about 20 shots, and over 500 species do it.

description:
A bombardier beetle blends two chemicals inside its body and fires the near-boiling spray in pulses.
It can pulse around 500 times a second.
